messages.summary:
## Objective
- Expand the existing playable folklore-creature game with a starter tutorial, pixel-art creature identities, a richer interconnected regional map, and water travel between Singapore and Indonesia.

## Requirements
- Add a small intro tutorial before choosing a starter.
- Give creatures pixel-art sprites and names related to their creature identity.
- Make the map more complex and interconnected, with a third-generation Pokémon-inspired feel.
- Represent Singapore and Malaysia as distinct map areas; provide ferry or Surf-like travel over water to Indonesia.
- Build a complete playable game without asking clarifying questions.

## Decisions
- Implemented a three-step tutorial covering the setting, movement/encounters, and strait travel.
- Made starters grant Surf travel access and added a ferry between Singapore’s Lantern Quay and the new Indonesian Nusa Kecil area.
- Reused the existing pixel-art sprite system and creature names already present in the game.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added tutorial flow before starter selection in `index.html`.
- Added a Nusa Kecil area and updated the location HUD for six areas.
- Added ferry boarding interaction between Singapore and Nusa Kecil; surfaced a ferry visual at relevant piers.
- Starters now enable Surf/ferry travel.

### Active
- Validate game behavior and visuals, including tutorial progression, movement between areas, ferry return travel, and encounter flow.
- Check whether the map feels sufficiently complex/interconnected and expand it if needed.
- Ensure all creature art and naming requirements are satisfied throughout the game UI.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect `index.html` and run the game in a browser to test tutorial, starter selection, Singapore/Nusa Kecil ferry travel, and controls.
2. Fix any runtime or navigation issues found; verify pixel-art sprites remain visible in all creature interfaces.
3. Save and inspect a current screenshot, then report assumptions and validation results.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Entire game implementation; tutorial, map, creatures, sprites, and ferry changes are here.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; no browser test or screenshot has been performed yet.
- Existing creature sprite data and names were already present before the latest edits.

## Objective
- Expand the existing folklore-creature game with a starter tutorial, pixel-art creatures, a richer interconnected regional map, and water travel between Singapore and Indonesia.

## Requirements
- Add a short intro tutorial before starter selection.
- Give creatures pixel-art sprites and names related to their identities.
- Make the map more complex and interconnected, with a third-generation Pokémon-inspired feel.
- Represent Singapore and Malaysia as distinct map areas; provide ferry or Surf-like travel to Indonesia.
- Deliver a complete playable game without clarifying questions.

## Decisions
- Use a three-step tutorial covering the setting, movement and encounters, and strait travel.
- Let the starter grant Surf access for ferry travel between Singapore’s Lantern Quay and Indonesia’s Nusa Kecil.
- Reuse the game’s existing pixel-art sprites and creature names.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added the tutorial flow before starter selection in `index.html`.
- Added Nusa Kecil and updated the location HUD for six areas.
- Added ferry boarding interactions and pier visuals for Singapore and Nusa Kecil.
- Starters now enable Surf/ferry travel.
- JavaScript syntax check passed with `node --check /tmp/opencode/game.js`; `git diff --check` reported no issues.

### Active
- Validate tutorial and starter selection, movement, encounters, and ferry travel in a browser.
- Inspect the map’s interconnectedness and verify creature art across interfaces.
- Capture and inspect a current screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Open the game in a browser and test tutorial progression, starter selection, movement and encounters.
2. Verify ferry travel in both directions and inspect pixel-art visibility and map connectivity; fix any issues.
3. Save and inspect a current screenshot, then summarize assumptions and validation results.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Entire game implementation, including tutorial, areas, sprites, and ferry.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; no browser test or screenshot has been completed.
- The HTML game server was started on port `3002`.
- `playwright-cli` and Chromium are available; JavaScript syntax validation passed.

## Objective
- Expand the folklore-creature game with a tutorial, pixel-art creatures, a richer interconnected regional map, and water travel between Singapore and Indonesia.

## Requirements
- Add a short intro tutorial before starter selection.
- Give creatures pixel-art sprites and identity-related names.
- Make the map more complex and interconnected, with a third-generation Pokémon-inspired feel.
- Represent Singapore and Malaysia as distinct areas; provide ferry or Surf-like travel to Indonesia.
- Deliver a complete playable game without clarifying questions.

## Decisions
- Use a three-step tutorial covering the setting, movement and encounters, and strait travel.
- Let the chosen starter grant Surf access for ferry travel between Singapore’s Lantern Quay and Indonesia’s Nusa Kecil.
- Reuse the game’s existing pixel-art sprites and creature names.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added the tutorial flow before starter selection, Nusa Kecil, ferry interactions, pier visuals, and starter-enabled Surf in `index.html`.
- Passed JavaScript syntax validation with `node --check /tmp/opencode/game.js` and `git diff --check`.
- Opened the game in a browser and verified the tutorial advances through all three pages, shows the starter choices, and selecting Bara starts the game with one companion.

### Active
- Validate movement, encounters, both ferry directions, and map connectivity in the browser.
- Inspect pixel-art visibility across interfaces and capture/inspect a current screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Test movement and encounters, then navigate to Singapore’s Lantern Quay and verify ferry travel to Nusa Kecil and back.
2. Inspect map connectivity and pixel-art visibility in the world and interfaces; fix any issues found.
3. Capture and inspect a current screenshot, then summarize validation results.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Entire game implementation, including tutorial, areas, sprites, and ferry.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; only `index.html` is modified.
- The browser is open at `http://127.0.0.1:3002`; tutorial and starter selection were tested through choosing Bara.
- Browser reported one missing-resource error for `http://127.0.0.1:3002/favicon.ico`; no other console errors or warnings were reported.
- A screenshot has not yet been captured; the earlier screenshot command failed because of its target syntax.

## Objective
- Expand the folklore-creature game with a tutorial, pixel-art creatures, a richer interconnected regional map, and water travel between Singapore and Indonesia.

## Requirements
- Add a short intro tutorial before starter selection.
- Give creatures pixel-art sprites and identity-related names.
- Make the map more complex and interconnected, with a third-generation Pokémon-inspired feel.
- Represent Singapore and Malaysia as distinct areas; provide ferry or Surf-like travel to Indonesia.
- Deliver a complete playable game without clarifying questions.

## Decisions
- Use a three-step tutorial covering the setting, movement and encounters, and strait travel.
- Let the chosen starter grant Surf access for ferry travel between Singapore’s Lantern Quay and Indonesia’s Nusa Kecil.
- Reuse the game’s existing pixel-art sprites and creature names.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added the tutorial flow before starter selection, Nusa Kecil, ferry interactions, pier visuals, and starter-enabled Surf in `index.html`.
- Verified tutorial progression and selecting Bara starts the game with one companion.
- Tested movement from Seruni Village to Singapore’s Lantern Quay and triggered a wild Kantilume encounter from tall grass; encounter UI appeared and “Give them space” closed it.
- Passed JavaScript syntax validation (`node --check /tmp/opencode/game.js`) and `git diff --check`.

### Active
- Validate movement and encounter flow further, reach the Lantern Quay pier, and test ferry travel to Nusa Kecil and back.
- Inspect map connectivity and pixel-art visibility in the world and interfaces; capture and inspect a current screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Navigate to the pier at Lantern Quay and verify ferry travel in both directions.
2. Check regional connectivity and sprite visibility across the world and interfaces.
3. Capture and inspect a screenshot, then summarize validation results.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Entire game implementation, including tutorial, areas, sprites, and ferry.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `git status --short` showed only `index.html` modified.
- Browser is open at `http://127.0.0.1:3002`; browser console only reported a missing `/favicon.ico` (404).
- Current browser run is in Lantern Quay; after moving right from the start to Singapore and down, the ferry prompt still showed “Look around,” so the pier has not yet been reached.
- The previous screenshot attempt failed with `Unexpected token "" while parsing css selector ""`; `playwright-cli screenshot` accepts a target and supports `--filename`.

## Objective
- Expand the folklore-creature game with a tutorial, pixel-art creatures, a richer interconnected regional map, and water travel between Singapore and Indonesia.

## Requirements
- Add a short intro tutorial before starter selection.
- Give creatures pixel-art sprites and identity-related names.
- Make the map more complex and interconnected, with a third-generation Pokémon-inspired feel.
- Represent Singapore and Malaysia as distinct areas; provide ferry or Surf-like travel to Indonesia.
- Deliver a complete playable game without clarifying questions.

## Decisions
- Use a three-step tutorial covering the setting, movement and encounters, and strait travel.
- Let the chosen starter grant Surf access for ferry travel between Singapore’s Lantern Quay and Indonesia’s Nusa Kecil.
- Reuse the game’s existing pixel-art sprites and creature names.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added the tutorial flow before starter selection, Nusa Kecil, ferry interactions, pier visuals, and starter-enabled Surf in `index.html`.
- Verified tutorial progression and selecting Bara starts the game with one companion.
- Tested movement from Seruni Village to Singapore’s Lantern Quay and triggered a wild Kantilume encounter from tall grass; encounter UI appeared and “Give them space” closed it.
- Passed JavaScript syntax validation (`node --check /tmp/opencode/game.js`) and `git diff --check`.
- Captured and inspected screenshots at `/tmp/opencode/lantern-quay.png`, `/tmp/opencode/map-current.png`, `/tmp/opencode/map-after-move.png`, `/tmp/opencode/map-check.png`, and `/tmp/opencode/after-controls.png`.

### Active
- Reliably reach the Lantern Quay pier and verify ferry travel to Nusa Kecil and back.
- Finish checking regional connectivity and pixel-art visibility in the world and interfaces.

### Blocked
- Ferry testing is pending: current browser is in Lantern Quay, but navigation attempts did not activate the ferry prompt; it still reads “✦ Look around”.

## Next Move
1. Determine the player’s current tile and navigate to a tile adjacent to `P` at Lantern Quay; verify the prompt and ferry travel in both directions.
2. Check regional connectivity and sprite visibility across the world and interfaces.
3. Re-run `git diff --check` and summarize validation results.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Entire game implementation, including tutorial, areas, sprites, and ferry.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; earlier `git status --short` showed only `index.html` modified.
- Browser is at `http://127.0.0.1:3002`; console reported one error, previously identified as a missing `/favicon.ico` (404).
- Browser snapshot confirms Lantern Quay, Singapore, Bara in the party, and the “Look around” prompt.
- Keyboard-event and pointer-event navigation attempts did not reach a ferry interaction; screenshots were saved under `/tmp/opencode/`.

## Objective
- Expand the folklore-creature game with a tutorial, pixel-art creatures, a richer interconnected regional map, and water travel between Singapore and Indonesia.

## Requirements
- Add a short intro tutorial before starter selection.
- Give creatures pixel-art sprites and identity-related names.
- Make the map more complex and interconnected, with a third-generation Pokémon-inspired feel.
- Represent Singapore and Malaysia as distinct areas; provide ferry or Surf-like travel to Indonesia.
- Deliver a complete playable game without clarifying questions.

## Decisions
- Use a three-step tutorial covering the setting, movement and encounters, and strait travel.
- Let the chosen starter grant Surf access for ferry travel between Singapore’s Lantern Quay and Indonesia’s Nusa Kecil.
- Reuse the game’s existing pixel-art sprites and creature names.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added tutorial flow before starter selection, Nusa Kecil, ferry interactions, pier visuals, and starter-enabled Surf in `index.html`.
- Verified tutorial progression and selecting Bara starts the game with one companion.
- Tested movement from Seruni Village to Singapore’s Lantern Quay and triggered a wild Kantilume encounter; “Give them space” closed the encounter.
- Passed JavaScript syntax validation (`node --check /tmp/opencode/game.js`) and `git diff --check`.

### Active
- Reach the Lantern Quay pier and verify ferry travel to Nusa Kecil and back.
- Check regional connectivity and pixel-art visibility across the world and interfaces.

### Blocked
- Ferry testing remains unverified: the browser is at Lantern Quay, but navigation attempts did not activate the ferry prompt; it still reads “✦ Look around”.

## Next Move
1. Inspect Lantern Quay’s player position and map collision/interact logic, then navigate to a tile adjacent to `P` and test travel in both directions.
2. Check regional connectivity and sprite visibility across the world and interfaces.
3. Re-run `git diff --check` and summarize validation.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Entire game implementation, including tutorial, areas, sprites, and ferry.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `git status --short` previously showed only `index.html` modified.
- Browser is at `http://127.0.0.1:3002`; console showed one error previously identified as missing `/favicon.ico` (404).
- Latest browser snapshot shows Lantern Quay, Singapore, Bara in the party, and the “Look around” prompt.

<subagent sessionID="ses_e1d59fd5dffeMdhcfeE3GUBjNT" state="completed">
## Architecture

The game is implemented in one file: [`/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html`]( /home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html ). It combines the markup, inline CSS, game data, canvas rendering, movement, battles, and UI updates.

## Best insertion points

- **World map and routes:** Extend the `areas` data and tile maps (around lines 30–37). `tileAt()`, `walkable()`, `draw()`, and `step()` (around lines 76–84 and 100) handle map lookup, collision, rendering, and movement. `ferry()` (around line 107) is the existing area-transfer mechanism.
- **Trainer rematches and gym progression:** Add progression/rematch state alongside the `trainers` data (around lines 69–75). `nearbyTrainer()` and `updatePrompt()` (around lines 79–80) handle trainer proximity and prompts; `talkTrainer()`, `battle()`, and `attack()` (around lines 95–97) handle encounters and victory rewards. Trainer defeat is currently a boolean, and there is no gym progression model.
- **Creature typing and sprites:** Creature records and starters are defined in `mons` and starter data (around lines 38–48); sprite pixel maps and palettes are around lines 50–63. `art()` and `paintArt()` (around lines 64–65) render creature art. Type labels also appear in the party, battle, starter, and guide UI, so adding a type involves updating both data and those presentation paths. Sprite names need corresponding entries in both sprite maps for `paintArt()` to render them.
- **Trainer avatar sprites:** The sidebar avatar is separate from the map characters: its `.avatar` markup is around line 19, with styling in the inline CSS around line 9. Player and NPC map icons are drawn as emoji in `draw()` (around lines 83–84); use that canvas rendering path for map avatar sprites.

## Risks to account for

- `draw()` owns map entities and canvas scaling; changes there can affect all map characters.
- Tile-coordinate assumptions are shared by `tileAt()`, `step()`, route maps, and ferry positions.
- `updateUI()` and `open()` regenerate UI content, so additions to those views need to be included in their render logic.
- CSS is compressed into long lines, with responsive overrides in the same style block.
</subagent>

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Complete `index.html` as a playable folklore-creature adventure with tutorial, regional maps, ferry travel, battles, and progression.
- Validate and repair map connectivity, interactions, and progression.

## Requirements
- Deliver a playable game without clarifying questions.
- Keep Singapore and Malaysia distinct; support ferry/Surf travel between Singapore and Indonesia.
- Connect the world vertically with wilderness routes and larger grass patches.
- Include a short tutorial, individual creature types and sprites, and a chibi trainer.

## Decisions
- Tutorial covers setting, movement and encounters, and strait travel.
- Starter grants Surf access for ferry travel between Lantern Quay and Nusa Kecil.
- Reuse existing folklore names and sprite style.
- Arrange six areas in a 3×2 layout with connecting route corridors.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added a three-step tutorial, starter selection, Singapore–Indonesia ferry flow, six-area world layout, Wayfinder sprite, type-effectiveness multipliers, trainer rematches, and three multi-match Spirit Trials gyms with badges and bosses.
- Added gym challenge UI; trials pause after each opponent with a Continue trial flow.
- Fixed synthesized route geometry in `tileAt`; reachability check confirmed all six areas and trainer positions are reachable.
- Fixed tutorial name entry so it persists when navigating Back and appears as the trainer name.
- Play-tested tutorial progression, starter selection, tea-stall purchases, and ferry travel in both directions. Singapore and Indonesia appear as distinct map regions.
- JavaScript syntax check and `git diff --check` passed before the latest small tutorial-name change.

### Active
- Continue testing encounters, type effects, trainer rematches, Spirit Trials progression, and additional interactions; fix issues found.
- Rerun JavaScript syntax and diff checks after latest change.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Continue Playwright testing in the existing browser session at `http://localhost:3002` for encounters, battles, type effectiveness, trainers, and gym progression.
2. Run JavaScript syntax and `git diff --check` validation.
3. Review the final diff and report results.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Single-file game implementation; currently modified and uncommitted.
- `/tmp/opencode/playwright.json`: Earlier Playwright configuration, though the CLI session is now accessible without `--config`.

## Important Context
- `git status --short` previously showed `M index.html`; latest tutorial-name fix remains uncommitted.
- World geometry uses `areaSpots=[[0,12],[16,0],[32,12],[16,12],[0,0],[32,0]]`, dimensions 48×24, and synthesized corridors at `y=5/17` and `x=8/24/40`.
- Successful ferry test: Lantern Quay → Nusa Kecil, Indonesia → Lantern Quay, Singapore.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Complete `index.html` as a playable folklore-creature adventure with tutorial, regional maps, ferry travel, battles, and progression.
- Validate and repair map connectivity, interactions, and progression.

## Requirements
- Deliver a playable game without clarifying questions.
- Keep Singapore and Malaysia distinct; support ferry/Surf travel between Singapore and Indonesia.
- Connect the world vertically with wilderness routes and larger grass patches.
- Include a short tutorial, individual creature types and sprites, and a chibi trainer.

## Decisions
- Tutorial covers setting, movement and encounters, and strait travel.
- Starter grants Surf access for ferry travel between Lantern Quay and Nusa Kecil.
- Reuse existing folklore names and sprite style.
- Arrange six areas in a 3×2 layout with connecting route corridors.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added a three-step tutorial, starter selection, Singapore–Indonesia ferry flow, six-area world layout, Wayfinder sprite, type-effectiveness multipliers, trainer rematches, and three multi-match Spirit Trials gyms with badges and bosses.
- Added gym challenge UI; trials pause after each opponent with a Continue trial flow.
- Fixed synthesized route geometry in `tileAt`; reachability check confirmed all six areas and trainer positions are reachable.
- Fixed tutorial name entry so it persists when navigating Back and appears as the trainer name.
- Play-tested tutorial progression, starter selection and name persistence, tea-stall purchases, and ferry travel in both directions; Singapore and Indonesia appear as distinct regions.
- Reran inline JavaScript syntax check (`node --check /tmp/opencode/game-check.js`) and `git diff --check`; both passed.

### Active
- Continue testing encounters, type effects, trainer rematches, Spirit Trials progression, and additional interactions; fix issues found.
- Review final diff and report results.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Continue browser testing at `http://localhost:3002` for encounters, type effectiveness, trainer rematches, and gym progression.
2. Finish the current Moonfern Gym battle sequence, then verify trial continuation and badge progression.
3. Review `git diff` and `git status`; report validation and results.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Single-file game implementation; modified and uncommitted.

## Important Context
- `git status --short` showed `M index.html`; latest changes remain uncommitted.
- World geometry uses `areaSpots=[[0,12],[16,0],[32,12],[16,12],[0,0],[32,0]]`, dimensions 48×24, and synthesized corridors at `y=5/17` and `x=8/24/40`.
- Ferry travel was verified both ways: Lantern Quay → Nusa Kecil, Indonesia → Lantern Quay, Singapore.
- Browser currently has a Moonfern Gym battle in progress against Tuyuli, the second trainer; starter is Rintik, and its HP has been depleted during battle.

Core:
  open [url]                  open the browser
  attach [name]               attach to a running playwright browser
  close                       close the browser
  detach                      detach from an attached browser
  goto <url>                  navigate to a url
  type <text>                 type text into editable element
  click <target> [button]     perform click on a web page
  dblclick <target> [button]  perform double click on a web page
  fill <target> <text>        fill text into editable element
  drag <startTarget> <endTarget> perform drag and drop between two elements
  drop <target>               drop files or data onto an element
  hover <target>              hover over element on page
  select <target> <val>       select an option in a dropdown
  upload <files...>           upload one or multiple files
  check <target>              check a checkbox or radio button
  uncheck <target>            uncheck a checkbox or radio button
  snapshot [target]           capture page snapshot to obtain element ref
  find [text]                 search the page snapshot for text or a regexp, returning matching nodes with surrounding context (like search snippets)
  eval <func> [target]        evaluate javascript expression on page or element
  dialog-accept [prompt]      accept a dialog
  dialog-dismiss              dismiss a dialog
  resize <w> <h>              resize the browser window
  delete-data                 delete session data

Navigation:
  go-back                     go back to the previous page
  go-forward                  go forward to the next page
  reload                      reload the current page

Keyboard:
  press <key>                 press a key on the keyboard, `a`, `arrowleft`
  keydown <key>               press a key down on the keyboard
  keyup <key>                 press a key up on the keyboard

Mouse:
  mousemove <x> <y>           move mouse to a given position
  mousedown [button]          press mouse down
  mouseup [button]            press mouse up
  mousewheel <dx> <dy>        scroll mouse wheel

Save as:
  screenshot [target]         screenshot of the current page or element

Tabs:
  tab-list                    list all tabs
  tab-new [url]               create a new tab
  tab-close [index]           close a browser tab
  tab-select <index>          select a browser tab

Storage:

  state-save [filename]       saves the current storage (authentication) state to a file
  cookie-list                 list all cookies (optionally filtered by domain/path)
  cookie-get <name>           get a specific cookie by name
  cookie-set <name> <value>   set a cookie with optional flags
  cookie-delete <name>        delete a specific cookie
  cookie-clear                clear all cookies
  localstorage-list           list all localstorage key-value pairs
  localstorage-get <key>      get a localstorage item by key
